stem: Magnesium shows reactions typical of a Group 2 metal.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw a labelled diagram to show the bonding in magnesium metal.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text: Identify the other products of reactions **1** and **2**.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Reaction **3** is used to form a precipitate of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ from $\text{MgCl}_2\text{(aq)}$.

State why $\text{Ca(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$ would **not** form a precipitate of $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ from $\text{BaCl}_2\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State the type of reaction that occurs in reaction **4**.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
$1\text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{MgCl}_2\text{(aq)}$ is placed in a test-tube. A few drops of $\text{AgNO}_3\text{(aq)}$ are added, followed by $1\text{ cm}^3$ of dilute $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$.

State in full what is observed in this experiment.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
When $1\text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{MgCl}_2\text{(aq)}$ is added to $1\text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)}$ in a test-tube, the solution remains orange.

Explain this observation.
